name: udt-authoring: pick a library-bearing biocontainer, not a bare image
description: Tier-2 check that UDT authoring reaches for an image that actually ships the library the tool imports. Asks for a pandas-based data-cleaning UDT -- the case that tempts `container: python:3.x-slim`, which cannot `import pandas`. This is the image-FAMILY decision, not tag resolution: the prompt says outright that the exact build tag will be verified separately, because with only skills_fetch exposed the agent has no resolver and the skill correctly tells it not to invent a tag it cannot verify. Without that framing a well-behaved agent would refuse to name an image at all and fail the assertion for the right reason. Asserts the agent (a) fetched the udt-authoring skill and (b) drafted a GalaxyUserTool whose `container:` value is a library-bearing image -- quay.io/biocontainers or the Galaxy singularity depot -- via a regex that tolerates YAML quoting, extra spacing, and a `docker://` prefix, so a correct answer isn't failed over punctuation. There is deliberately no `mustNotInclude: ["container: python:"]` to go with it, for the same reason udt-authoring-threads has no hardcoded-thread-count ban: an absence check over chat text is anti-correlated with the understanding being measured. A model that internalized the lesson is likely to WRITE the mistake in order to warn against it ("don't use `container: python:3.12-slim`, it can't import pandas") and would be scored FAIL for exactly the right reasoning, while the ban still misses `docker.io/library/python`, `continuumio/miniconda3`, and every other spelling. The positive check is the robust proxy -- if the container line names a biocontainer, it isn't a bare language image. Mirrors the container dimension of Galaxy's custom_tool eval (galaxyproject/galaxy#22968, #22981).
inputs: Wrap a small data-cleaning step as a Galaxy user-defined tool for my own account: read a tab-separated file with pandas, drop the rows where the `score` column is empty, and write the cleaned table back out. Draft the full GalaxyUserTool YAML definition -- show me the complete definition, don't create it on the server yet. Don't worry about pinning an exact container build tag; I'll verify the exact tag myself before we create it. Just make sure the image you name is the right one for this tool.
